name: DesktopSideBar has horizontal scroll
description:
## Summary

1. The desktop sidebar (`src/components/layout/DesktopSidebar.vue`) showed a horizontal scrollbar because its scroll area had `overflow-y-auto` without `overflow-x-hidden`, so any oversized child produced an X-axis scrollbar.
2. The main culprit was the header row in `AppsSection.vue`, where `ProjectDetailt` (`w-full`) plus two sibling icon buttons exceeded the 256px sidebar width.
3. Root cause of the extra width was missing `min-w-0` on `truncate` spans, so long project/workspace names could never shrink and truncated.
4. Fix applied: `min-w-0 overflow-x-hidden` on both scroll containers, `min-w-0` on the header row and name spans, `flex-1 min-w-0` for the selector, and `shrink-0` on the icon buttons.
5. Five files were modified (`DesktopSidebar.vue`, `AppsSection.vue`, `ProjectDetailt.vue`, `PinnedProjectsSwitcher.vue`, `WorkspacesSection.vue`), with the noted trade-off that `tooltip-right` hints are now clipped at the sidebar edge.

messages.content: DesktopSideBar has horizontal scroll, fix it, it must fit to the width

I'll start by locating the `DesktopSideBar` component and understanding its structure.Let me read the `DesktopSidebar.vue` component.Now let me examine the child components that render inside the sidebar, since horizontal overflow usually originates there.Let me read the remaining sidebar child components that could introduce width overflow.Let me look at how the sidebar is placed in the app shell to understand the containing layout.Let me find the app shell and how `DesktopSidebar` is mounted.Let me check the previous version of the sidebar and the `Modal` component (rendered inline by `ProjectDetailt`).I've completed my investigation. Let me summarize the root cause before proposing the fix. ## 1. Analysis & Pre-Thinking **Core Requirements** - The desktop sidebar (`src/components/layout/DesktopSidebar.vue`) shows a **horizontal scrollbar**. - It must instead **fit its content to the fixed sidebar width** (`w-64` = 256px expanded / `w-16` collapsed). **Root cause** 1. The scrollable area uses `class="flex-1 overflow-y-auto flex flex-col"`. Because `overflow-x` stays `visible` while `overflow-y` is not, the browser computes `overflow-x: auto`. So *any* child wider than 256px produces a horizontal scrollbar. 2. The offending child is the header row in `AppsSection.vue`: ```html
``` `ProjectDetailt`'s root is `w-full` (flex-basis 100%) **plus** two sibling buttons, and its project-name `` has **no `min-w-0`**. In flexbox a `truncate` span only truncates if it can shrink below its content width, so long project names keep the button at its full (untruncated) width → the row grows past 256px → horizontal overflow. 3. Same truncation pattern (no `min-w-0`) exists in `PinnedProjectsSwitcher.vue` (pinned project names) and `WorkspacesSection.vue` (workspace names) — both inside the same scroll area. **Strategic Approach** - Make text that is already marked `truncate` actually able to shrink (`min-w-0`), so the name fits instead of pushing the row wide. - Let the project-selector flex item shrink (`flex-1 min-w-0`) and stop the icon buttons from being squashed (`shrink-0`). - Add `overflow-x-hidden` to the sidebar scroll area as a guarantee that no horizontal scrolling can occur (this also stops daisyUI `tooltip-right` pseudo-elements from adding scroll width on hover). **Dependencies & Risks** - `ProjectDetailt` is reused elsewhere (TopBar, Knowledge, Workspace views). Adding `min-w-0` is purely additive: it only *allows* shrinking, it never forces it, so other layouts are unaffected. - `overflow-x-hidden` clips content that would otherwise overflow sideways — with the truncation fixes nothing important overflows, so this is safe. **Target Files** - `src/components/layout/DesktopSidebar.vue` (scroll area) - `src/components/layout/AppsSection.vue` (header row) - `src/components/layout/ProjectDetailt.vue` (truncation) - `src/components/layout/PinnedProjectsSwitcher.vue` (truncation) - `src/components/layout/WorkspacesSection.vue` (truncation) ## 2. Minimum Changes Approach - **`DesktopSidebar.vue`**: on both scroll containers (mobile + desktop) add `min-w-0 overflow-x-hidden` so the area can never scroll horizontally. - **`AppsSection.vue`**: row → `min-w-0`; `ProjectDetailt` → `flex-1 min-w-0`; pin button & `ViewModeToggle` → `shrink-0`. - **`ProjectDetailt.vue`**: root div, button and name span get `min-w-0` so the name truncates. - **`PinnedProjectsSwitcher.vue`**: name span gets `min-w-0`. - **`WorkspacesSection.vue`**: name span gets `min-w-0`. ## 3.
